funfact_topics.text: Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold (the Mpemba effect)
Helium was discovered on the Sun before it was ever found on Earth. In 1868 astronomers Pierre Janssen and Norman Lockye
The word 'quarantine' comes from the Venetian quaranta giorni (forty days), the ship isolation period used in Black Death Venice.
Sea otters raft together and wrap in kelp (or hold paws) while sleeping to avoid drifting apart on the current.
The largest living organism on Earth is a honey fungus (Armillaria ostoyae) in Oregon's Blue Mountains, spanning about 9.6 sq km and estimated to be up to roughly 8,650 years old.
Point Nemo is so remote the nearest humans are often astronauts in orbit
Pluto has not completed a single orbit around the Sun since its 1930 discovery; its orbital period is about 248 years.
Butterflies taste with their feet via chemoreceptors on their tarsi.
Carrots were originally purple, white or yellow; the orange carrot was bred by Dutch growers, first recorded in 1721, and gets its colour from beta-carotene.
The world’s first webcam was created in 1991 to watch the Trojan Room coffee pot at the University of Cambridge.
Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light because compounds in their exoskeleton, including beta-carboline, fluoresce; field researchers hunt them at ni
A day on Venus is longer than its year: it rotates once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225.
Hawaiian pizza was invented in Canada by Sam Panopoulos (1962), not in Hawaii or the US.
The word OK began as an 1839 joke spelling of 'oll korrect' (all correct).
Bluetooth wireless technology is named after Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson, the 10th-century Danish king who unified Denma
Russia spans 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad to Chukotka - more than any other country.
Africa is the only continent that lies in all four hemispheres.
Bananas are mildly radioactive because of potassium-40 (banana equivalent dose).
Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth, growing up to about 91 cm in a day.
The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire.
Fresh pineapple contains bromelain, a protein-digesting enzyme, so eating a lot can make your mouth feel raw; heat destroys it, so tinned pineapple does not bite back.
Wombats are the only animals that produce cube-shaped droppings
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The shortest war in history lasted about 40 minutes (Anglo-Zanzibar War, 1896).
A teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh about a billion tonnes.
The mantis shrimp has up to 16 types of colour photoreceptor and strikes with cavitation-bubble force.
The Dead Sea is salty enough (about 34%) that swimmers float and almost nothing lives in it.
In a group of 23 people, two probably share a birthday

The world's shortest scheduled passenger flight links the Orkney islands of Westray and Papa Westray in Scotland, a hop of about 2.7 kilometres. Operated by Loganair, it is timetabled at roughly 90 se
A hummingbird is the only bird that can fly backwards; its heart can beat past 1,200 times a minute.
Scotland's national animal is the mythical unicorn
The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer heat

Koalas have fingerprints so similar to a human's that even under a microscope they can be hard to tell apart. The looping, whorled ridges evolved independently from ours — close relatives like wombats and kangaroos lack them — most likely to help the animals grip and handle eucalyptus leaves.
Saturn is less dense than water (~0.69 g/cm3) and would float in a big enough bath.
Human skin emits an ultraweak metabolic glow, ~1000x too dim to see (2009 study).
Vantablack, a coating of vertical carbon nanotubes, absorbs about 99.965% of visible light, so an object coated in it looks like a flat black void.
Lobster was so plentiful in colonial New England it was poor people's food, fed to prisoners and used as fertilizer, before becoming a delicacy in the 1800s.
Sharks are older than trees: shark-like scales date to ~450 Mya, the first true trees to ~385-370 Mya.
The shortest war in history lasted about 38 minutes
Until about 5,000 years ago the Sahara was green (the African Humid Period), driven by Earth's orbital precession.
Flamingos hatch grey and turn pink only from carotenoid pigments in the algae and brine shrimp they eat.
The dot over an i or j is called a tittle
The Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 centimetres a year; measured since 1969 via Apollo laser reflectors, the retreat also gradually lengthens Earth's day.
Most 'wasabi' served outside Japan is not wasabi but a dyed paste of horseradish and mustard; real Wasabia japonica is hard to grow and loses its pungency within ~15 minutes of grating.
The Canary Islands are named after dogs (Latin Canariae Insulae), not the canary bird.
The equals sign (=) was invented in 1557 by Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde, who chose two equal-length parallel lines because nothing could be more equal.
Cashews are sold shelled because their raw double shell contains urushiol, the caustic oil in poison ivy.
An octopus has three hearts and blue blood
Botanically bananas, grapes, tomatoes and avocados are berries, while strawberries and raspberries are not.
In the 1830s US, ketchup was sold as medicine: tomato pills touted as a cure for indigestion.
A lightning bolt superheats air to about 30,000 K, roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface (~5,800 K).
The first computer 'bug' was a literal moth found in the relay of Harvard's Mark II in 1947.
The word 'robot' was coined for Karel Capek's 1920 Czech play R.U.R., from Czech 'robota' (forced labour).
A newborn has about 300 bones but an adult has only 206; many fuse as we grow.
Shuffling a 52-card deck almost certainly makes an order never seen before (52! permutations).
There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way (2015 Nature study: ~3 trillion trees vs ~100-400 billion stars).
Gallium is a metal that melts in your hand at about 29.8C, just below body temperature.
